items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the correction law, in relation to people in the custody of the department of corrections and community supervision and a medical authorization form to disclose private medical information
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S5428

TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the correction law, in relation to people in the
custody of the department of corrections and community supervision and
a medical authorization form to disclose private medical information

PURPOSE:

This bill would require the department of corrections and community
supervision (DOCCS) to provide inmates with forms to disclose medical
information and mental health treatment information, and to provide
persons appointed to receive such disclosures a copy of the
authorization form.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section one of the bill requires DOCCS to provide forms to disclose
medical information and mental health treatment information to inmates
upon their arrival at a reception facility and each transfer to a new
facility so that inmates may opt to appoint a family member or other
person to receive such information.

Section two of the bill requires DOCCS to provide copies of such
disclosure forms to the person designated by an inmate. DOCCS shall
provide such person protected health information as governed by HIPAA
or as governed by mental hygiene law.

Section three of the bill is the effective date.

JUSTIFICATION:

There are more than 8,000 men and women under state custody who
receive treatment for mental illness, and there are approximately
10,000 inmates under the age of 25, some of whom have significant
medical conditions for which they received treatment prior to their
commitment to a state correctional facility. Parents, as well as
spouses, often find it very difficult to communicate with the
Department about the mental health or medical condition of their loved
ones. Disclosure forms signed by inmates may have expired, may never
have been signed, may have been difficult to obtain, or may not have
travelled with the inmate as intended to the medical facility or
mental health unit in which an inmate has been placed. Without signed
release forms, DOCCS and OMH will not give any medical or mental
health information to an inmate's family. This difficulty in
communicating with DOCCS becomes particularly crucial when inmates are
in medical units, outside hospitals, or have attempted suicide.
During these times the family may wish to obtain information from
DOCCS or OMH and may also provide valuable information that may help
with the Department's effort to treat the inmate appropriately.

At a time of crisis it is often too late for the Department, the
inmate and the family, guardian or person closest to the inmate to
execute a disclosure form that would allow the Department to
communicate with the family about the status of the inmate. This bill
would resolve the issue by requiring the Department to provide


disclosure forms as a matter of routine to all inmates upon arrival at
a reception facility and upon transfer to new facilities throughout
their incarceration, as well as providing a copy to the person
authorized by the inmate to receive information. The disclosure forms
may be declined, edited or revoked at any time by the inmate.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New Bill

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

Negligible cost to the state.

EFFECTIVE DATE:

This act shall take effect on the one hundred twentieth day after it
shall have become a law. Effective immediately, the addition,
amendment and/or repeal of any rules or regulations necessary for the
implementation of the foregoing section of this act on its effective
date is authorized to be made on or before such effective date.
